subject: MediQ evaluation: success signals, trigger ladder, and acceptance tests
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@mediqhealth.com>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@mediqhealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP + proposed acceptance checks for the MediQ evaluation

Hi Emily / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Attached is our draft mutual action plan (MediQ_MAP_v1.2.xlsx) and a short list of candidate acceptance tests. I tried to keep the acceptance criteria measurable and light-weight so you can validate quickly during the 4-week evaluation.

High-level proposal (please skim the attached for detail):
- Success signals: 95% intent-to-action concordance on the 500-sample test set; average inference latency < 350ms P50 in your staging region; no classification regressions > 2% on labeled set.
- Exit gates (must be satisfied to be green): functional pass on the 5 smoke tests; infra/hard-failure tolerance — system recovers from a simulated node loss without > 2x latency degradation; security checklist items 1–6 cleared (SOC evidence).
- Acceptance tests: automated smoke harness (5 scenarios), load test (50 concurrent flows for 10 minutes), qualitative sampling of edge cases (20 examples each).

Questions for you:
1) Can we align on the 4-week cadence starting Monday 9/6?
2) Any regulatory/security artifacts you need from our side (SOC/pen test timelines)?
3) Are there preferred cut points where you want manual checkpoints vs automatic pass/fail?

Next steps I propose: finalize the MAP worksheet (I added an owners column), lock the 4-week timeline, schedule a short weekly sync with Priyom and Grace for technical gating.

Attachments: MediQ_MAP_v1.2.xlsx; service-level-profiles.pdf; evidence-checklist.csv

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if you prefer to walk through the sheet.

—
Avery Johnson
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0182

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@mediqhealth.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@mediqhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + proposed acceptance checks for the MediQ evaluation

Thanks Avery — we reviewed the attachments with the engineering and compliance teams. Overall looks sensible. A few quick notes:

- Timeline: the 4-week cadence works for us but can we start the formal evaluation window on 2026-09-07 (week after your proposed date) — gives us time for procurement sign-off.
- Success thresholds: request that the latency target be P95 < 450ms (we have a higher P95 sensitivity under load), keep P50 target as you suggested.
- Exit gate addition: add a privacy/data residency check for exported logs (we need confirmation that logs do not include PHI in free-text snapshots).
- Acceptance test tweak: for the qualitative edge-case sampling, can we expand to 30 examples and include 10 labeled by our clinical SMEs?

Also, our procurement team will need a single-point contact to triage contract redlines — cc'ing Rajiv (he's our procurement lead).

If that sounds ok, we can lock dates and level-set on who runs which tests.

Best,
Emily Zhao
Head of Product, MediQ Health
emily.zhao@mediqhealth.com | +1 617-555-0219

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@mediqhealth.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + proposed acceptance checks for the MediQ evaluation

Emily — thanks for the quick review and the constructive tweaks. A few engineering clarifications so the acceptance tests are executable:

1) Latency targets: we can guarantee P50 < 350ms and P95 < 450ms in your staging region under the proposed test load (50 concurrent flows) if we keep sequence lengths to the 95th-percentile of your sample distribution. We'll add a test-run that includes the 99th percentile sequences so you can see tail behavior.
2) Privacy: our default logs redact free-text responses and only capture metadata (request id, model id, token counts, latency). We'll provide a short tech note that explains the redaction and the retention window (30 days for staging logs by default — we can extend if required).
3) Edge-case sampling: we can expand to 30 examples including 10 annotated by your SMEs. Grace will coordinate the labeling checklist and provide an evaluation rubric.

I'll update the MAP sheet with test owners (automation: Redwood QA; qualitative: MediQ SMEs + Redwood SRE) and add a new exit gate row for log residency/privacy validation.

Proposed timeline update:
- 2026-09-07: procurement signed + environment access granted
- 2026-09-08 to 2026-09-28: evaluation window (3 weeks active testing + 1 week buffer for evidence and close)
- 2026-10-01: decision checklist and contract signature target

If that timeline fits, I'll update the sheet and create the runbook for the smoke tests.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwoodinference.com

Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + proposed acceptance checks for the MediQ evaluation

Emily / Rajiv —

Appreciate the quick alignment. Summary of what we'll lock into the MAP and runbook (updated sheet attached):

Agreed items:
- Evaluation window: 2026-09-08 through 2026-09-28 (3 weeks active test + 1 final week for evidence collection).
- Success signals: P50 < 350ms; P95 < 450ms; intent-to-action concordance >= 95% on the 500-sample labeled set; regression delta <= 2% vs baseline.
- Exit gates: pass automated smoke harness (5 scenarios); privacy residency verification (no free-text PHI in exported logs); infra resilience test (single node loss recovery within 2x baseline latency).
- Acceptance tests: automated smoke (Redwood QA), load test (Redwood + MediQ run together, 50 concurrent flows), edge-case sampling (30 examples, 10 labeled by MediQ SMEs).

Owners:
- Redwood: test automation, smoke harness, load test orchestration, tech note on log redaction (Priyom).
- MediQ: SME labeling, compliance verification, procurement sign-off (Emily / Rajiv).

Procurement and legal: Rajiv, thanks for stepping in — please let us know the required contract redline turnaround so we can keep the 10/01 decision target.

Next actions I committed to today:
1) Publish the updated MAP with owners & timeline (done — see attached MediQ_MAP_v1.2.xlsx).
2) Upload the smoke-runbook to the shared Drive folder and add the test checklist.
3) Priyom will circulate the technical note on log handling by 2026-09-02.

If there are no objections, we'll treat this as the working plan and kick off the environment access requests on 2026-09-01.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth evaluation.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0182
